mechanism_fit: This is M8, a cross-caller convention conflict. The callee is StrMatcher.StringMatcher.isMatch(char[], int, int, int). Its first javadoc sentence reads like a boolean ("Returns whether or not the given text matches the stored string"), but it actually returns the number of characters matched, which is 2 for "}}". The gold, StrSubstitutor.substitute(StrBuilder,int,int,List), is the trigger's caller. Its faulty line treats a suffix hit as a one-character marker: it uses pos++ where the correct line is pos += endMatchLen. That one-character reading looks natural there because the no-match branch a few lines above also does pos++, and the default suffix "}" is a single character. Other callers of the same callee use the return value as a length, and passing tests cover them with multi-character matchers: StrBuilder.replaceImpl(StrMatcher,...) with stringMatcher("cb"), and StrTokenizer.readWithQuotes with stringMatcher("IGNORE"). The callee's own tests also assert a return value of 2. The trigger output "Hi Bob}." fits three explanations: isMatch returning too small a length, StrBuilder.replace removing one character too few, or substitute advancing too little. The validator's G9 run showed that one-line edits to StrBuilder.replace do make the trigger pass but break the existing suite, so the existing tests settle who owns the fault.

Fault: in the suffix-match branch where nestedVarCount == 0, `pos += endMatchLen;` is changed to `pos++;`. The minimal repair restores `pos += endMatchLen;`.

ownership_reason: StringMatcher.isMatch returns the number of characters it matched (2 for "}}"). Its @return says so, its body returns chars.length, and StrMatcherTest.testStringMatcher_String and testMatcherIndices assert 2 for a two-character matcher. The other callers of this callee use the value as a length, and passing multi-character tests cover them: StrBuilder.replaceImpl(StrMatcher,...) removes removeLen characters (testReplace_StrMatcher_String_int_int_int_VaryMatcher with "cb"), and StrTokenizer.readWithQuotes skips ignoredLen characters (testBasicIgnoreTrimmed4 with "IGNORE"). StrBuilder.replace(int,int,String) removes exactly [startIndex, endIndex), as testReplace_int_int_String pins. StrSubstitutor.resolveVariable documents endPos as the end of the variable including the suffix. substitute is the only method that turns a suffix match into endPos. It advances by one character (pos++) instead of by endMatchLen, unlike its own prefix handling (pos += startMatchLen). So with a two-character suffix, endPos stops inside the suffix and one suffix character survives. Restoring pos += endMatchLen fixes the trigger and keeps the suite green. Any one-line edit to isMatch or StrBuilder.replace that hides the stray character breaks the passing tests above.
trigger: org.apache.commons.lang3.text.StrSubstitutorTest::testDoubleBraceMarkers is appended to src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/StrSubstitutorTest.java (JUnit 4 @Test, no new imports). concerns:
1. There is local evidence inside the gold itself. substitute handles the prefix with pos += startMatchLen, its nested-suffix branch still does pos += endMatchLen, and the variable endMatchLen sits right next to the faulty pos++. A model can therefore find the gold by comparing lines within the method, without the cross-caller evidence, so the instance may be easier than the recipe intends.
2. The callee's convention is also stated locally: the @return line says "the number of matching characters", and StrMatcherTest asserts 2 directly. Only the first javadoc sentence suggests a boolean reading. Earlier notes found little definer bias when the callee's own docs state the convention.
3. isMatch has many callers, not just two. The second callers named here (StrBuilder.replaceImpl, StrTokenizer.readWithQuotes) are in different classes from the gold.
4. Unrelated to this instance: pristine Lang-1f has a latent bug in CharSequenceTranslator.translate, which calls codePointAt(input, pt) where it should use pos. This trigger never reaches it.
